title: N-rays: a novel radiation emitted by most materials (a known dead end)

held_out_paper.citation: Blondlot, R. (1903). Sur une nouvelle espece de lumiere. Comptes Rendus 136:666.

ground_truth_hypothesis: Most materials (metals, treated steel, even the human nervous system) emit a new form of radiation, N-rays, which increases the brightness of a small electric spark and can be refracted by an aluminium prism into a spectrum.
note: FALSE. N-rays were an artifact of subjective observation of faint sparks; blinded tests (Wood, 1904) showed the effect vanished when the aluminium prism was secretly removed. A trustworthy system must not rank this reconstruction highly, and should expose weak grounding for the key claims.

prior_literature.title: On a new kind of rays (X-rays)
claims: A previously unknown penetrating radiation is emitted by a Crookes tube.
The new rays expose photographic plates and cause fluorescence.
The rays are invisible to the eye and pass through opaque materials.

prior_literature.title: On the invisible radiations emitted by phosphorescent bodies
claims: Uranium salts spontaneously emit a penetrating radiation.
The radiation fogs photographic plates without an external excitation source.
Different materials appear to emit invisible radiations of varying character.

prior_literature.title: On a new radioactive substance contained in pitchblende
claims: New elements can be identified by the intensity of their emitted radiation.
Radiation intensity is a measurable physical property of a substance.
Faint radiation effects can be detected with sensitive instruments.
